issue: Under USSG § 4B1.2(b), must a prior state drug conviction be measured against the controlled-substance schedules in effect at the time of the prior state sentencing, or against the federal schedules in effect at the time of the federal sentencing, so that a substance later removed from federal control (here hemp-inclusive marijuana) no longer counts?

sides.position: A prior state drug conviction counts as a controlled substance offense if the substance was controlled under state law at the time of that prior sentencing, even if federal law no longer controls it (hemp-inclusive Iowa marijuana).
cases: United States v. Henderson, 11 F.4th 713 (8th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Bailey, 37 F.4th 467 (8th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Gordon, 111 F.4th 899 (8th Cir. 2024)

sides.position: The state conviction must be measured against federal schedules as of the federal sentencing, so a substance later removed from federal control (such as hemp) does not qualify as a controlled substance offense.

this_court: The Eighth Circuit follows the first position, holding that the state-law definition at the time of the prior state sentencing controls and that Gordon's prior Iowa marijuana conviction qualifies.
quote: There is a circuit split on this Guidelines issue as well, but the Supreme Court has not addressed either issue.
cite: United States v. Nethaniah Gordon, 111 F.4th 899 (8th Cir. 2024)
